_README: Rules used by Claims Lab. Each rule maps wording patterns to a specific paragraph of 21 CFR 101.93 or 21 U.S.C. 343(r)(6). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions; a space matches any whitespace, and each pattern is wrapped in word boundaries unless boundaries is false. The fdaExample fields quote FDA's Small Entity Compliance Guide. These rules detect wording patterns: they are not a regulatory determination, and a sentence with no match is not cleared. Corrections welcome by pull request, with a citation.

guide.label: FDA Small Entity Compliance Guide on Structure/Function Claims

g1.text: Definition of disease — excludes diseases resulting from essential nutrient deficiencies (e.g. scurvy, pellagra)

g2i.text: Has an effect on a specific disease or class of diseases

g2ii.text: Has an effect on the characteristic signs or symptoms of a specific disease or class of diseases

g2iii.text: Has an effect on an abnormal condition associated with a natural state or process

g2iv.text: Has an effect on a disease through the product name, formulation, citations, use of the term disease, or pictures

g2v.text: Belongs to a class of products intended to diagnose, mitigate, treat, cure, or prevent a disease

g2vi.text: Is a substitute for a product that is a therapy for a disease

g2vii.text: Augments a particular therapy or drug action intended to diagnose, mitigate, treat, cure, or prevent a disease

g2viii.text: Has a role in the body's response to a disease or to a vector of disease

g2ix.text: Treats, prevents, or mitigates adverse events associated with a therapy for a disease

r6.text: A structure/function statement may not claim to diagnose, mitigate, treat, cure, or prevent a specific disease or class of diseases

r6A.text: A benefit claim related to a classical nutrient deficiency disease must disclose the prevalence of that disease in the United States

r6B.text: The manufacturer must have substantiation that the statement is truthful and not misleading

a.text: FDA must be notified no later than 30 days after first marketing a product bearing the statement

f.text: Structure/function statements are permitted only if they do not claim to diagnose, mitigate, treat, cure, or prevent disease

structureFunction.reason: Describes the role of a nutrient or ingredient in the body's normal structure or function — the kind of statement 21 CFR 101.93(f) permits, subject to the requirements below.

disclaimer.evaluated: (this statement has|these statements have) not been evaluated by the food and drug administration
disclaimer.intended: this product is not intended to diagnose,? treat,? cure,? (or|and) prevent any disease
disclaimer.singular: This statement has not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.
disclaimer.plural: These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.

notChecked: Images, symbols and colours on the pack. FDA counts pictures, vignettes and symbols toward an implied disease claim under (g)(2)(iv); this tool reads text only.
Product names in context. Only names built around cure or an obvious condition are caught.
The catch-all criterion, (g)(2)(x) — anything that otherwise suggests an effect on disease.
Health claims and nutrient content claims, which follow separate rules in 21 CFR 101.14 and 101.13.
Advertising outside the label, which falls under the FTC.
Disclaimer placement and typography under 101.93(d) and (e) — only whether its wording is present.
Anything outside its word lists. A claim with no flags has not been cleared.

Lowering cholesterol is a characteristic effect on disease. FDA treats "reduces cholesterol" as a disease claim.
rules.rewrite: Supports cholesterol levels already within a normal range
rules.fdaExample: maintain cholesterol levels that are already in the normal range (acceptable) vs reduces cholesterol (disease claim)

rules.reason: Lowering blood pressure is a characteristic effect on disease.
rules.rewrite: Supports blood pressure already within a normal range

rules.reason: Lowering blood sugar is a characteristic effect on disease.
rules.rewrite: Supports healthy glucose metabolism already within a normal range

rules.reason: An effect so closely tied to disease that FDA treats any claim about it as a disease claim.
rules.fdaExample: inhibits platelet aggregation
rules.noRewrite: There is no structure/function version of a claim about this condition. Remove the reference.

rules.reason: Regulating or controlling a disease marker can imply correcting an abnormal level. Tie it to levels already in the normal range.
rules.rewrite: Supports healthy levels already within a normal range

rules.reason: "Anxiety" can describe a diagnosable disorder. FDA has accepted "relieves stress and frustration" as a structure/function claim; wording about anxiety is likely to be read as a disease claim.
rules.fdaExample: relieves stress and frustration (acceptable)

rules.reason: Inflammation is a common sign of disease. FDA's example "reduces inflammation (rheumatoid arthritis)" is a disease claim.
rules.fdaExample: improves joint mobility and reduces inflammation (rheumatoid arthritis)

rules.reason: Pain relief reads as an analgesic effect, and pain is a characteristic sign of many diseases.
rules.rewrite: Supports recovery from occasional muscle soreness after exercise

rules.reason: FDA accepts claims about occasional sleeplessness, but not persistent sleeplessness, which reads as insomnia.
Clinically low testosterone is a medical condition.
rules.rewrite: Supports healthy testosterone levels already within a normal range

rules.reason: FDA gives cystic acne as an abnormal condition — a disease claim. Noncystic acne is acceptable.
rules.fdaExample: cystic acne (disease) vs noncystic acne (acceptable)

rules.reason: An abnormal condition associated with a natural state.
rules.noRewrite: There is no structure/function version of a claim about this condition. Remove the reference.

rules.reason: FDA accepts "mild memory loss associated with aging" but not claims about serious cognitive impairment.
rules.rewrite: Helps with mild memory loss associated with aging
rules.fdaExample: mild memory loss associated with aging (acceptable)

rules.reason: Severity language can turn a normal condition into an abnormal one. FDA accepts mild conditions associated with natural states.
rules.rewrite: Use "mild" or "occasional" and tie it to the natural state

rules.reason: Uses the word disease about the product's effect.
rules.fdaExample: Promotes good health and prevents the onset of disease
rules.noRewrite: Remove the reference to disease. General statements like "a good diet promotes good health" are acceptable because they aren't about the product.

rules.reason: A product name built around "cure" implies a disease claim.
rules.fdaExample: CircuCure
rules.noRewrite: Rename the product without cure, treat, correct or prevent.

rules.reason: A product name that evokes a disease implies a disease claim.
rules.fdaExample: CarpalHealth
rules.noRewrite: Rename the product without reference to the condition.

rules.reason: References an ingredient regulated as a drug and known for treating disease.
rules.fdaExample: listing aspirin or digoxin as an ingredient
rules.noRewrite: There is no structure/function version of a claim about this condition. Remove the reference.

rules.reason: The Rx symbol is not automatically a disease claim, but FDA says it may misbrand the product if the context suggests a prescription drug.
rules.noRewrite: Remove the Rx symbol unless the context is clearly unrelated to prescription drugs.

rules.reason: Names a class of products that treat or prevent disease.
rules.fdaExample: analgesic, antibiotic, antidepressant, antimicrobial, antiseptic, antiviral, vaccine
rules.noRewrite: Remove the drug-class term. Describe the structure or function the product supports instead.

rules.reason: A drug-like class term. FDA accepts "diuretic that relieves temporary water-weight gain" because the context is clearly structure/function.
rules.rewrite: Tie the term explicitly to a normal, temporary effect
rules.fdaExample: diuretic that relieves temporary water-weight gain (acceptable)

patterns: (alternative to|instead of|replacement for|substitute for|replaces?|better than|as effective as|works like)( [a-z]+){0,2} (prescriptions?|medications?|meds|drugs?|pills|antidepressants?|statins?|ssris?|sleeping pills|painkillers|chemotherapy|chemo|aspirin|ibuprofen|acetaminophen|paracetamol|naproxen|digoxin|metformin|atorvastatin|warfarin|prozac|xanax|viagra|cialis|valium|ambien|adderall|zoloft|lexapro|ozempic|wegovy|mounjaro|lipitor|celebrex)
rules.reason: Positions the product as a replacement for a therapy that treats disease.
rules.fdaExample: claims that a product substitutes for a disease therapy
rules.noRewrite: Remove the comparison to a drug or therapy.

rules.reason: Names a prescription drug, implying the product substitutes for it.
rules.noRewrite: Remove the reference to the drug.

patterns: (works with|enhances|boosts|amplifies|complements|increases the effect of|improves the effect of)( the (effects?|action) of)?( your)? (medications?|prescriptions?|chemotherapy|chemo|radiation( therapy)?|statins?|antidepressants?|drug therapy|cancer treatment)
rules.reason: Claims to augment a therapy intended to treat disease.
rules.fdaExample: useful in providing nutritional support (acceptable, because it does not mention the therapy)
rules.noRewrite: Remove the reference to the therapy.

rules.reason: Describes a role in the body's response to disease or a disease vector. FDA accepts "supports the immune system" because it is not specific to disease.
rules.fdaExample: supports the body's ability to resist infection (disease claim) vs supports the immune system (acceptable)

rules.reason: Tying immune support to cold or flu season implies preventing those diseases.
Claims to mitigate adverse effects of a therapy for disease. FDA does accept counterbalancing nutrient depletion caused by a drug.
rules.fdaExample: to maintain the intestinal flora in people on antibiotics
rules.noRewrite: If the product counterbalances a nutrient depleted by a drug, say that specifically. Otherwise remove the reference.

rules.reason: Drug language. The statute bars structure/function statements from claiming to diagnose, mitigate, treat, cure or prevent disease; FDA notes these words can create an implied disease claim depending on context.
rules.noRewrite: Replace with structure/function language such as supports, maintains or promotes.

rules.reason: FDA lists "prevent" among words that may create an implied disease claim depending on context.
rules.noRewrite: Replace with structure/function language such as supports or maintains.

rules.reason: A classical nutrient deficiency disease is excluded from the definition of disease, so a claim about it is not a disease claim. It must disclose how prevalent the disease is in the United States.
rules.noRewrite: Keep the claim and add the U.S. prevalence disclosure.

rules.reason: Makes a specific evidentiary promise. Every structure/function claim needs substantiation before it is made; wording like this raises what that substantiation has to support.
rules.noRewrite: Keep only if your evidence supports this exact wording.
